morningSummary:
Saturday, 21 November 2026 — Morning News & Global Update. Updated at 06:57 Europe/Paris. Presented by Sophie Laurent.

NIGERIA — The Federal High Court has rejected Atiku Abubakar and the ADC's application to amend their pre-election case against President Bola Tinubu. This was a procedural ruling on the proposed amendment, not a final decision on the underlying allegations; the substantive matter was reported as fixed for 2 December. In Bayelsa, police say four people, including two children, died and 24 were rescued after a boat carrying mourners capsized; searches and investigations continue. All 36 state assemblies have approved the proposed state-police constitutional amendment, but presidential assent and implementation steps remain outstanding. Vice-President Kashim Shettima has urged lenders to widen affordable finance for farmers and small businesses. The CBN's reported OMO allotments have exceeded ₦90tn in 2026; this is a gross figure, not the net amount withdrawn after maturities.

AFRICA — Search operations continue after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal. Local officials told AP that one body had been recovered and several people were missing; estimates of the number aboard differ.

EUROPE — Russia launched a large drone and missile assault on Ukraine. Ukrainian officials reported eight deaths. Poland said three Russian objects violated its airspace; NATO described the incident as dangerous and investigations are continuing.

WORLD — The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya under the Genocide Convention; Myanmar rejected the ruling. US technology shares plunged on Friday, with the S&P 500 down 3.7% and the Nasdaq down 5.3%. President Trump says Iran wants a deal, but no agreement has been announced.

EDITORIAL NOTE — Allegations are attributed to the parties making them. The Atiku ruling is not a final judgment on the substantive suit. Casualty figures are attributed to police or local authorities and may change. Contextual images are labelled; where no verified image was available, no substitute image has been used.

breaking.title: Four dead and 24 rescued after boat carrying mourners capsizes in Bayelsa
breaking.imageNote: No verified photograph of this specific accident was available in the RadiantWaves repository at publication time; the story is intentionally published without an illustrative image.
breaking.summary: Police say four people, including two children, died and 24 passengers were rescued after a boat carrying mourners to a burial capsized in Southern Ijaw on Friday. Search-and-rescue work and an investigation are continuing.
breaking.content: The Bayelsa State Police Command said the passenger boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it developed a mechanical fault and capsized near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities at about 11 a.m. on 20 November. Police said four bodies—two adults and two children—had been recovered and 24 people rescued. Five injured survivors were taken to a hospital in Yenagoa, while others received treatment locally. Police said the boat manager was in custody for investigation and the operator had reportedly fled. The total number of people aboard and the full casualty figure had not been established in the police update. The cause remains under investigation.
breaking.source: Bayelsa State Police Command, reported by Punch, 20 November 2026; Reuters, 20 November 2026

breaking.title: All 36 state assemblies approve proposed state-police constitutional amendment
breaking.imageNote: Contextual photograph of Nigeria's legislature; not a photograph of the state assemblies' approval announcement.
breaking.summary: The Clerk to the National Assembly says all 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police Services. Presidential assent and further legal and operational steps are still required.
breaking.content: The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, said the verification process had been completed and that the State Police Services amendment had received approval from all 36 state assemblies, exceeding the constitutional threshold of 24. The proposal would amend the 1999 Constitution to provide a framework for state-controlled police services alongside the federal police. The Clerk said the bill was ready for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. Approval by state assemblies does not mean state police are already operational: the constitutional process must be completed and implementing laws, safeguards, funding and accountability arrangements would still be needed.
breaking.source: Statement by the Clerk to the National Assembly, reported by The Star, 17 November 2026; Business Times Nigeria, 16 November 2026

breaking.title: World Court finds Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya
breaking.imageAlt: United Nations and international justice, contextual image
breaking.imageNote: Contextual international-justice image from the RadiantWaves repository; not a photograph of the ICJ courtroom or the judgment session.
breaking.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled on 19 November that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during the 2017 operations in Rakhine State. The United Nations welcomed the judgment; Myanmar rejected it.
breaking.content: In The Gambia v. Myanmar, the International Court of Justice found that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention in its treatment of the Rohingya during the 2017 clearance operations. UN Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed the judgment and described it as the first time the Court had found a state responsible for committing genocide. The Court's ruling concerns state responsibility under the Genocide Convention; it is not a criminal conviction of individual military commanders. Myanmar's Foreign Ministry rejected the judgment, citing the 9–6 division among judges and disputing the Court's assessment. The practical test will be compliance, protection of Rohingya people, accountability and conditions for safe, voluntary return.

worldNews.content: In The Gambia v. Myanmar, the International Court of Justice found that Myanmar violated the Genocide Convention in its treatment of the Rohingya during the 2017 clearance operations. UN Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed the judgment and described it as the first time the Court had found a state responsible for committing genocide. The Court's ruling concerns state responsibility under the Genocide Convention; it is not a criminal conviction of individual military commanders. Myanmar's Foreign Ministry rejected the judgment, citing the 9–6 division among judges and disputing the Court's assessment. The practical test will be compliance, protection of Rohingya people, accountability and conditions for safe, voluntary return.

articles.title: Court rejects Atiku and ADC bid to amend suit challenging Tinubu's 2027 eligibility
articles.summary: The Federal High Court in Abuja has rejected Atiku Abubakar and the ADC's application to amend their pre-election case against President Bola Tinubu. The ruling concerns the proposed amendment, not the final merits of the underlying allegations.
articles.content: Justice Inyang Ekwo ruled on 20 November that the proposed changes would introduce new facts and alter the character of the pre-election case after the defendants had responded. The application was opposed by Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress and INEC. The original case concerns Atiku and the ADC's challenge to Tinubu's eligibility, including allegations relating to his NYSC discharge certificate. Tinubu and the APC have denied wrongdoing. The court's ruling on the amendment application does not itself establish that the certificate was forged, nor does it amount to a final determination of the substantive suit. THISDAY reported that the substantive matter was fixed for 2 December. Separately, the ADC leadership dispute arising from the 5 November judgment remains before the Court of Appeal: the Mark-led faction says it has filed a 17-ground appeal and sought a stay, while a rival faction has asserted that the Federal High Court judgment should be implemented. INEC has not announced a final public determination of the rival claims.
articles.imageNote: Existing RadiantWaves portrait of Atiku; it is an archive portrait, not a photograph of the 20 November court proceedings.
articles.source: Channels Television, 20 November 2026; TheCable, 20 November 2026; THISDAY, 20 November 2026; Punch, 18–19 November 2026
articles.whyItMatters: The decision is an important procedural development in a high-profile pre-election case, but it must not be misreported as a final ruling on the underlying allegations.
articles.whatHappensNext: The substantive eligibility case was reported as fixed for 2 December. The ADC leadership appeal and any stay application remain separate proceedings.

articles.title: Four dead and 24 rescued after boat carrying mourners capsizes in Bayelsa
articles.summary: Police say four people, including two children, died and 24 passengers were rescued after a boat carrying mourners to a burial capsized in Southern Ijaw on Friday. Search-and-rescue work and an investigation are continuing.
articles.content: The Bayelsa State Police Command said the passenger boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it developed a mechanical fault and capsized near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities at about 11 a.m. on 20 November. Police said four bodies—two adults and two children—had been recovered and 24 people rescued. Five injured survivors were taken to a hospital in Yenagoa, while others received treatment locally. The practical test will be compliance, protection of Rohingya people, accountability and conditions for safe, voluntary return.

asiaNews.title: Trump, Xi and Putin summit ends without a breakthrough on Ukraine

asiaNews.content: The leaders met on the sidelines of the APEC gathering in Shenzhen on 19 November. Reporting described discussions on nuclear risks, Ukraine and international security. Their joint declaration said nuclear war must never be fought and called for wider international cooperation, but it did not establish a new arms-control framework or a ceasefire in Ukraine. The absence of Ukraine from the meeting is significant because the country is directly affected by any settlement. The summit's statements should not be described as a peace agreement.

businessNews.content: The Central Bank has used open-market operations to manage liquidity and inflation risks ahead of the 2027 elections. The figure describes gross securities allotments; maturities and other liquidity movements affect the net impact on the banking system. The CBN's objective is to contain excess liquidity and inflationary pressure, but the effect on lending rates, government financing and private-sector credit will depend on the broader monetary and fiscal environment.

businessNews.title: AI-led sell-off pushes US stocks deeper into correction territory
businessNews.summary: A sharp technology and AI share sell-off sent the S&P 500 down 3.7% and the Nasdaq down 5.3% on Friday. The S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory, while the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains.
businessNews.content: Associated Press reported that US shares fell sharply on 20 November as investors questioned AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the path to profitability. The S&P 500 dropped 3.7%, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the Dow declined 1.9%. Nvidia fell 14%, adding to pressure on semiconductor and AI-related companies. A correction is commonly defined as a fall of at least 10% from a recent peak. The sell-off reflects market repricing and uncertainty; it does not by itself prove that the AI sector's long-term prospects have ended.

editorial.title: A landmark genocide judgment must lead to protection and accountability
editorial.imageAlt: United Nations and international justice, contextual image
editorial.imageNote: Contextual image; not the ICJ courtroom or the Rohingya community.
editorial.summary: The ICJ's finding of state responsibility for genocide against the Rohingya is historic. Its meaning will be measured by protection, accountability, reparations and safe, voluntary return.
editorial.content: The International Court of Justice's 19 November judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar is a landmark finding under the Genocide Convention. It is not a criminal conviction of individual commanders, and it cannot by itself guarantee safety for Rohingya people who remain displaced. Governments and international institutions should now focus on compliance, humanitarian access, preservation of evidence, reparations and conditions for safe, voluntary return. The judgment must not be reduced to symbolism.
editorial.source: International Court of Justice; United Nations, 19 November 2026

analysis.title: The AI market correction: repricing expectations, not a verdict on the technology
analysis.imageNote: Contextual AI infrastructure image, not a stock-exchange photograph.
analysis.summary: Friday's sell-off shows how quickly high expectations can be repriced when investors question capital spending, earnings and interest rates.
analysis.content: The Nasdaq's 5.3% fall and the S&P 500's 3.7% decline on 20 November reflect concerns about valuations, the scale of AI infrastructure spending and the timing of returns. The market move should not be treated as proof that AI investment has ended. Investors will look for evidence of durable revenue, productivity gains and manageable financing costs. For households and businesses, the immediate lesson is that technology hype and market prices can move differently from the underlying pace of innovation.

publicInterestFeature.title: Nigeria's electricity crisis: the need for transparent grid information
publicInterestFeature.summary: Reports of generation falling to around 3,180MW underline the pressure on homes and businesses. Consumers need clear, timely information from operators and regulators.
publicInterestFeature.content: A grid-generation figure is a snapshot, not a guarantee of supply in every area. Authorities should publish the causes of shortfalls, explain gas and transmission constraints, and provide realistic restoration information. DisCos should communicate allocation and outage schedules transparently. Long-term improvement requires reliable generation, transmission investment, payment discipline and accountable regulation.

sportsNews.title: FIFA appoints Daniel Amokachi and four others to NFF normalisation committee
sportsNews.summary: FIFA has named former Super Eagles captain Daniel Amokachi among five members of a committee tasked with managing the Nigeria Football Federation and overseeing governance reforms ahead of new elections.
sportsNews.content: FIFA has appointed lawyer Sampson Ebomhe as chairman of a five-member NFF Normalisation Committee. The other members are sports administrator and journalist Godwin Enakhena, former Nigeria captain and two-time FIFA World Cup player Daniel Amokachi, Amina Yerima and Joe Abah. The members are expected to assume their duties immediately, subject to eligibility checks by FIFA's Review Committee. Their mandate includes managing the federation's daily affairs, reviewing NFF statutes and electoral rules with FIFA and CAF, proposing governance reforms and organising fresh elections. The committee's mandate must end no later than 31 May 2027. FIFA has stated that members will not be eligible to contest the upcoming NFF elections.
